records.text: White has gained a passed pawn. Do not confuse freedom from enemy pawns ahead with freedom from all resistance.
Black has gained a passed pawn. Do not confuse freedom from enemy pawns ahead with freedom from all resistance.
The stronger move would have given White a passed pawn. That possibility deserves attention.
The stronger move would have given Black a passed pawn. That possibility deserves attention.
White now has an isolated pawn. No friendly pawn stands on either adjacent file; piece support must be judged on its own.
Black now has an isolated pawn. No friendly pawn stands on either adjacent file; piece support must be judged on its own.
With the better move, White would have an isolated pawn. Stronger play does not always mean a tidier pawn structure.
With the better move, Black would have an isolated pawn. Stronger play does not always mean a tidier pawn structure.
White's pawns now share a file. Doubled pawns are a structural fact, not a verdict on the position.
Black's pawns now share a file. Doubled pawns are a structural fact, not a verdict on the position.
The better move would have doubled White's pawns. Judge that structure alongside the whole position.
The better move would have doubled Black's pawns. Judge that structure alongside the whole position.
White's rook now occupies an open file. No pawns remain on that file; pieces still matter.
Black's rook now occupies an open file. No pawns remain on that file; pieces still matter.
The stronger alternative would have placed White's rook on a pawnless file. An open file is not an automatic invasion.
The stronger alternative would have placed Black's rook on a pawnless file. An open file is not an automatic invasion.
White's rook has a half-open file: enemy pawns remain, friendly pawns do not. Assess the resistance before assuming entry.
Black's rook has a half-open file: enemy pawns remain, friendly pawns do not. Assess the resistance before assuming entry.
With the stronger move, White's rook would have had a half-open file. Only enemy pawns would remain on it.
With the stronger move, Black's rook would have had a half-open file. Only enemy pawns would remain on it.
White's knight has gained a defender. Its former lack of support has been addressed.
Black's knight has gained a defender. Its former lack of support has been addressed.
White's bishop is defended now, having stood unguarded. Count that change precisely.
Black's bishop is defended now, having stood unguarded. Count that change precisely.
White's rook no longer stands undefended. A guard is present; complete safety is a different question.
Black's rook no longer stands undefended. A guard is present; complete safety is a different question.
White's queen has acquired protection it lacked. Even a queen needs its defenders counted.
Black's queen has acquired protection it lacked. Even a queen needs its defenders counted.
The better move would have supplied a defender for White's unguarded knight. That is a concrete change in support.
The better move would have supplied a defender for Black's unguarded knight. That is a concrete change in support.
White's bishop would have gained its missing guard with the stronger move. Include that in the comparison.
Black's bishop would have gained its missing guard with the stronger move. Include that in the comparison.
The stronger alternative would have defended White's previously unguarded rook. Support must not be overlooked.
The stronger alternative would have defended Black's previously unguarded rook. Support must not be overlooked.
A defender for White's queen was possible with the better move. It would no longer have stood unguarded.
A defender for Black's queen was possible with the better move. It would no longer have stood unguarded.
White's knight has lost all its defenders. Examine the replies and establish whether it can be taken.
Black's knight has lost all its defenders. Examine the replies and establish whether it can be taken.
White's bishop has lost its last guard. That change must be accounted for.
Black's bishop has lost its last guard. That change must be accounted for.
White's rook is now undefended after losing its protection. A serious detail to examine, not proof of a loss.
Black's rook is now undefended after losing its protection. A serious detail to examine, not proof of a loss.
White's queen no longer has a defender. Strength of movement does not replace support.
Black's queen no longer has a defender. Strength of movement does not replace support.
The stronger move would have left White's knight without a defender. Better moves still require exact accounting.
The stronger move would have left Black's knight without a defender. Better moves still require exact accounting.
With the better alternative, White's bishop would have lost its last guard. Undefended need not mean lost.
With the better alternative, Black's bishop would have lost its last guard. Undefended need not mean lost.
White's rook would have lost all its protection under the stronger alternative. The whole position decides the consequence.
Black's rook would have lost all its protection under the stronger alternative. The whole position decides the consequence.
The better move would have left White's queen without protection. Examine the replies before judging the cost.
The better move would have left Black's queen without protection. Examine the replies before judging the cost.
The knight leaves its original square. Development has begun for that piece; its next duties remain to be judged.
A first move for this knight. Bringing a piece out is the beginning of its deployment.
The knight begins its deployment by leaving its original square. Its placement deserves scrutiny.
The knight's initial deployment is made. Judge its placement as well as its departure.
The bishop leaves its starting post for the first time. Development is a step, not a completed plan.
A bishop begins its deployment. The original square is behind it now.
The bishop makes its first departure from home. Now assess its new position.
This bishop's development starts with its first move from the original square. Consider where it belongs next.
The stronger move would have begun this knight's development. It would have left its original square.
A knight's first departure from home was available with the better move. Examine where that choice would place it.
With the stronger alternative, a knight would have made its initial move from its starting square.
The better choice would have brought an undeveloped knight off its home square. Compare that deployment.
The stronger alternative would have started a bishop's development. Its first departure was available.
A bishop would have left its original square under the better move. That was a different deployment.
The better choice would have brought a bishop out for the first time. Examine that placement closely.
With the stronger move, an undeveloped bishop would have left home. That possibility merits examination.
Below the standard available here. The move gives up value compared with the stronger choice.
A stronger move was possible. This choice leaves a worse position; study the difference before moving on.
This decision concedes more than it needed to. Set the better move beside it and examine the difference.
The position could have been handled more strongly. The shortfall lies in the choice just made.
A capture is available in the immediate reply. It belongs in the calculation, whether or not it proves profitable.
The opposing side can capture next. Account for that response before judging this move.
An immediate capture must be considered. Availability alone does not establish a gain.
The next reply can take something. Calculate the capture before assigning it a value.
The opponent erred, and you answered with punishment. That is how a chance should be used.
You made the previous mistake count against the opponent. Good; an offered chance needs an answer.
The opponent's last error did not go unchallenged. You took advantage of it.
The stronger choice deserves a direct comparison with this move.
There was a better alternative. Examine what that choice would change.
A more exact move was available here; that is the comparison to make.
The passed pawn advances toward promotion. Distance gained is not promotion secured.
A passer has been pushed farther forward. The final rank is closer, but resistance still needs calculation.
The strongest response is a check. Begin the reply calculation with the king's obligation.
Check comes with the best reply. That immediate demand must be met.
Correct for this lesson. Continue with the same attention.
The instructed move, delivered. Proceed.
That matches the lesson's intended move. Keep to the task.
The move is correct. The puzzle still demands another answer.
Good so far. Finish the remaining puzzle work.
That part is solved. Continue; the puzzle is still in progress.
The studied opening move is in place. That is accurate recall.
Correct for this repertoire. The recalled move matches the material.
You supplied the opening answer from the study. Accepted.
The strongest choice here. Precision earns its credit.
Best. The move meets the highest standard in this position.
Sound play, though a stronger choice remained. Good is the proper judgment.
A good move. It holds up, but it is not the strongest available.
